# `silk/crypto/ed25519`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Ed25519 signatures with 32-byte keys and 64-byte signatures (RFC 8032).

## When to use
Use [`Ed25519PrivateKey`](#Ed25519PrivateKey) to sign messages, and [`Ed25519PublicKey`](#Ed25519PublicKey) to check that a message
was signed by the holder of a known Ed25519 key, such as a release signing key.

## Details
[`Ed25519PrivateKey.fromSeed`](#Ed25519PrivateKey.impl.fromSeed) takes the 32-byte seed that RFC 8032 calls the private key, and
[`Ed25519PrivateKey.generate`](#Ed25519PrivateKey.impl.generate) makes a new one. Signing is deterministic: the same key and
message give the same signature. It multiplies by secret scalars in constant time.

`Ed25519PublicKey.fromBytes` decodes and checks the public key once. `verify` borrows the message and the
signature, requires the scalar half of the signature to be below the group order, and checks
the cofactorless equation `[S]B = R + [k]A` with `k = SHA-512(R || A || M) mod L`. Arithmetic
uses bounded local storage, without an allocator.

## Gotchas
Secrets are not erased. Verification works on public data and does not try to run in constant
time. A valid
signature proves only that the key holder signed these exact bytes. For prehashed formats, such
as minisign's `ED` algorithm, pass the digest as the message.

## Examples
### Reject a signature over a different message
```silk
import silk.crypto.ed25519 {Ed25519PublicKey}
import silk.core.result {Result}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // RFC 8032 section 7.1, test 1: the empty message.
  let key: [u8; 32] = [
    215, 90, 152, 1, 130, 177, 10, 183, 213, 75, 254, 211, 201, 100, 7, 58,
    14, 225, 114, 243, 218, 166, 35, 37, 175, 2, 26, 104, 247, 7, 81, 26,
  ]
  let signature: [u8; 64] = [
    229, 86, 67, 0, 195, 96, 172, 114, 144, 134, 226, 204, 128, 110, 130, 138,
    132, 135, 127, 30, 184, 229, 217, 116, 216, 115, 224, 101, 34, 73, 1, 85,
    95, 184, 130, 21, 144, 163, 59, 172, 198, 30, 57, 112, 28, 249, 180, 107,
    210, 91, 245, 240, 89, 91, 190, 36, 101, 81, 65, 67, 142, 122, 16, 11,
  ]
  let empty: [u8; 0] = []
  let other: [u8; 1] = [0]
  return match Ed25519PublicKey.fromBytes(&key) {
    Result.Failure { error } => 1
    Result.Success { value: verifier } => {
      let accepted = match verifier.verify(&empty, &signature) {
        Result.Success { value } => true
        Result.Failure { error } => false
      }
      let forged = match verifier.verify(&other, &signature) {
        Result.Success { value } => true
        Result.Failure { error } => false
      }
      if !accepted || forged {
        return 2
      }
      return 0
    }
  }
}
```

### Sign a message and verify it
```silk
import silk.crypto.ed25519 {Ed25519Error, Ed25519PrivateKey, Ed25519PublicKey}
import silk.core.result {Result}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // A fixed seed for the example. Real programs use `Ed25519PrivateKey.generate`.
  let seed: [u8; 32] = [42; 32]
  let key = match Ed25519PrivateKey.fromSeed(&seed) {
    Result<Ed25519PrivateKey, Ed25519Error>.Success { value } => move value
    Result<Ed25519PrivateKey, Ed25519Error>.Failure {..} => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let signature = key.sign(b"hello")
  return match Ed25519PublicKey.fromBytes(&key.publicKey()) {
    Result<Ed25519PublicKey, Ed25519Error>.Failure {..} => 2
    Result<Ed25519PublicKey, Ed25519Error>.Success { value: verifier } => {
      match verifier.verify(b"hello", &signature) {
        Result<(), Ed25519Error>.Success {..} => 0
        Result<(), Ed25519Error>.Failure {..} => 3
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Import as `Ed25519PublicKey` with `import silk.crypto.ed25519 { Ed25519PublicKey }`.

<a id="Ed25519PrivateKey"></a>

## `Ed25519PrivateKey`

```silk
pub struct Ed25519PrivateKey
```

An Ed25519 private key that signs messages (RFC 8032).

### When to use
Make it from a 32-byte seed with [`Ed25519PrivateKey.fromSeed`](#Ed25519PrivateKey.impl.fromSeed), or make a new one with
[`Ed25519PrivateKey.generate`](#Ed25519PrivateKey.impl.generate). Then call [`Ed25519PrivateKey.sign`](#Ed25519PrivateKey.impl.sign).

### Details
The seed is what RFC 8032 calls the private key, and what PKCS #8 stores for Ed25519. The key
keeps the seed, the clamped secret scalar, the nonce prefix, and the public key. Signing is
deterministic and runs in constant time for the secret values.

### Gotchas
Secrets are not erased.

<a id="Ed25519PrivateKey.impl.sign"></a>

### Method `sign`

```silk
pub fn sign(self: &Self, message: &[u8]) -> [u8; 64]
```

Returns the 64-byte Ed25519 signature of `message`, `R` followed by `S`.

The signature is deterministic: `r = SHA-512(prefix || M) mod L`, `R = [r]B`,
`k = SHA-512(R || A || M) mod L`, and `S = (r + k a) mod L`.

<a id="Ed25519PublicKey"></a>

## `Ed25519PublicKey`

```silk
pub struct Ed25519PublicKey
```

A decoded Ed25519 public key, for signature verification (RFC 8032).

### When to use

Use it to check that a message was signed by the holder of a known Ed25519 key, such as a
release signing key. Decode the key once with [`Ed25519PublicKey.fromBytes`](#Ed25519PublicKey.impl.fromBytes), then call
[`Ed25519PublicKey.verify`](#Ed25519PublicKey.impl.verify). To sign, use [`Ed25519PrivateKey`](#Ed25519PrivateKey).

### Gotchas

Verification works on public data and does not try to run in constant time. A valid signature
proves only that the key holder signed these exact bytes. For prehashed formats, such as
minisign's `ED` algorithm, pass the digest as the message.

<a id="Ed25519PublicKey.impl.verify"></a>

### Method `verify`

```silk
pub fn verify(self: &Ed25519PublicKey, message: &[u8], signature: &[u8]) -> Result<
    (),
    Ed25519Error
  >
```

Checks that `signature` is this key's Ed25519 signature of `message`.

It borrows the message and the signature, requires the scalar half of the signature to be
below the group order, and checks the cofactorless equation `[S]B = R + [k]A` with
`k = SHA-512(R || A || M) mod L`. It does not allocate.

#### Gotchas
It does not try to run in constant time. A valid signature proves only that the key holder
signed these exact bytes. For prehashed formats, such as minisign's `ED` algorithm, pass the
digest as the message.

#### Errors
`InvalidSignatureLength` when `signature` is not 64 bytes long, and `InvalidSignature` when
its scalar is not below the group order or the verification equation does not hold.
